items.title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
items.one_liner: Rendering documents as images offers multimodal models conditional protection against prompt injection, but does not completely eliminate risks.
items.summary: Research into indirect prompt injection attacks on multimodal language models demonstrates that rendering untrusted text documents as page images provides conditional protection against prompt hijacking. items.one_liner: Secure long-horizon LLM agent execution harnesses against state-transfer failures and prompt injections using hash-chained audit records.

items.title: Who Is Behind the Harness? Verifying Model Identity in Coding Agents through Behavioral Fingerprinting
items.one_liner: LIDAR black-box fingerprinting identifies coding-agent LLMs based on runtime decisions and tool interactions.
items.summary: Replacing the underlying large language model in coding-agent harnesses can alter critical security decisions like failure recovery and code verification. Because traditional text-based LLM fingerprints fail when mediated by agent system prompts and execution frameworks, researchers propose LIDAR (LLM Identification from Decisions and Actions at Runtime). LIDAR evaluates execution behavior using active black-box probes across three harnesses without requiring model weights or logit access. Evaluations show high closed-set Top-1 accuracy between 91.39% and 98.89%, proving that agent decision trajectories expose reliable model-identity evidence.
items.bottom_line: Coding-agent execution behavior and decision trajectories can accurately identify underlying LLMs without inspecting model weights.
